framework.name: NIST AI Risk Management Framework
framework.issuing_body: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
framework.description: A voluntary framework for managing AI risks to individuals, organisations, and society. Provides a structured approach through four core functions — GOVERN, MAP, MEASURE, MANAGE — each with categories and subcategories. Designed for flexibility across sectors, use cases, and risk levels. Complementary to ISO 42001 and the EU AI Act.

requirements.title: GOVERN 1.1 — Policies and Procedures for AI Risk
requirements.text: Policies, processes, procedures, and practices across the organisation related to the mapping, measuring, and managing of AI risks are in place, transparent, and implemented effectively.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Establish documented policies and procedures for AI risk management across the organisation
evidence_needed: Procedures for risk identification and treatment

controls.description: Ensure AI risk policies are communicated, trained on, and implemented consistently

requirements.title: GOVERN 1.2 — Accountability for AI Risk
requirements.text: Accountability structures are in place for AI risk management so that individuals and organisational units are accountable for AI risk decisions. Roles and responsibilities include those from development to deployment.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Define and document accountability for AI risk decisions at system and portfolio level
Establish an AI governance body or committee with documented terms and cadence

requirements.title: GOVERN 1.3 — Organisational Teams and Culture
requirements.text: Organisational teams are committed to a culture that considers and communicates AI risk. Teams have diverse backgrounds, skills, and expertise to contribute to AI risk management from development through deployment.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Build AI risk management teams with diverse technical, ethical, legal, and domain expertise

requirements.title: GOVERN 2.1 — AI Risk Tolerance
requirements.text: Organisational risk tolerances are determined and communicated, and serve as inputs for AI system risk determinations. Risk tolerance statements are specific to AI use cases and updated as AI contexts change.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Define and document AI risk tolerance statements at organisational and system level

requirements.title: GOVERN 3.1 — AI Risk Workforce
requirements.text: AI risk management knowledge, skills, and abilities exist throughout the organisation. Personnel understand their AI risk responsibilities and have access to appropriate training and development.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Assess and address AI risk management competency gaps across the workforce

requirements.title: GOVERN 4.1 — Organisational Teams Reflecting Society
requirements.text: Organisational teams developing, deploying, and overseeing AI systems represent diverse backgrounds and lived experiences. Diverse perspectives are actively sought in AI design, development, deployment, and governance.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Implement practices to ensure diverse and inclusive AI teams

requirements.title: GOVERN 5.1 — Organisational Policies for Third-Party AI
requirements.text: Organisational policies and practices are in place for third-party AI entities, including vendors, AI developers, deployers, operators, and other AI supply chain actors. Due diligence processes address AI risk in procurement and contracting.
requirements.scope: All AI deploying organisations using third-party AI

controls.description: Establish AI vendor due diligence and risk assessment processes
Include AI risk provisions in third-party contracts
evidence_needed: AI contract templates with risk clauses

requirements.title: GOVERN 6.1 — Policies for AI Risk in Acquisition
requirements.text: Policies and procedures are in place for AI procurement and acquisition such that AI risk is evaluated in the procurement process and appropriate risk management requirements are passed to AI suppliers.
requirements.scope: All AI deploying organisations

controls.description: Embed AI risk assessment in the procurement lifecycle

requirements.title: MAP 1.1 — AI System Context
requirements.text: Context is established for the AI risk assessment. This includes understanding the intended purpose, potential harms, and benefits of the AI system; the deployment context; affected individuals and groups; and the regulatory and policy environment.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Document intended use, deployment context, and affected populations for each AI system
Map applicable regulatory requirements to each AI system

requirements.title: MAP 1.5 — AI System Organisational Risk Priorities
requirements.text: Organisational risk priorities are understood and documented. AI risk assessments are aligned with organisational risk management practices and enterprise risk frameworks.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Integrate AI risk into enterprise risk management frameworks

requirements.title: MAP 2.1 — Scientific Basis for AI Use Case
requirements.text: The scientific basis for the AI system's use case is understood and documented. Assumptions, constraints, and limitations are known and communicated to relevant stakeholders.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Document the technical and scientific basis for the AI system including assumptions and known limitations

requirements.title: MAP 3.1 — AI System Risk Identification
requirements.text: Risks of the AI system in the context of intended deployment are identified and catalogued. Potential harms to individuals, groups, and society are enumerated. Positive impacts are also identified.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Maintain a risk catalogue for each AI system covering harms to individuals, groups, and society
Identify and document potential for disparate impacts across demographic groups

requirements.title: MAP 5.1 — Likelihood and Impact of AI Risks
requirements.text: Likelihood and magnitude of each identified AI risk is estimated and documented. Risk prioritisation is based on a combination of likelihood and impact, with higher priority given to risks affecting fundamental rights and safety.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Apply consistent risk scoring methodology to estimate likelihood and impact of AI risks

requirements.title: MEASURE 1.1 — AI Risk Measurement Approaches
requirements.text: Approaches and metrics for measuring AI risks are established and agreed upon. Measurement methods are appropriate for the AI use case and risk level. Both quantitative and qualitative measures are used.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Define quantitative and qualitative metrics for AI risk measurement per system

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.1 — AI System Testing and Evaluation
requirements.text: Test sets that reflect the intended operational environment are used to evaluate AI system performance and trustworthiness before deployment. Testing includes adversarial testing, bias testing, and performance across diverse population subgroups.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Conduct pre-deployment testing across representative and adversarial scenarios
Evaluate model performance across demographic subgroups and document disparate performance

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.2 — AI System Explainability
requirements.text: AI system outputs can be explained in a manner consistent with the intended deployment context and use case. Explainability methods are documented and appropriate to the risk level and audience (technical and non-technical stakeholders).
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Implement and document explainability approaches appropriate to the model type and use case
Validate that explanations are meaningful and actionable for the intended audience

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.5 — AI System Bias and Fairness
requirements.text: Bias and fairness assessments are conducted and documented. Assessment covers statistical bias in training data, algorithmic bias in model design, and deployment bias in the operational context. Findings inform mitigation measures.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Conduct structured bias assessments covering training data, model algorithm, and deployment context

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.6 — AI System Security
requirements.text: The AI system is evaluated for cybersecurity risks including adversarial attacks, data poisoning, model inversion, and prompt injection. Security testing is conducted before deployment and on an ongoing basis.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers

controls.description: Conduct AI-specific security testing including adversarial robustness evaluation

requirements.title: MEASURE 2.7 — AI System Privacy
requirements.text: Privacy risks of the AI system are identified and evaluated. Assessments cover personal data used in training and inference, potential for re-identification, and differential privacy considerations.
requirements.scope: AI developers and deployers using personal data

controls.description: Conduct privacy risk assessment for AI systems using personal data

requirements.title: MEASURE 4.1 — Post-Deployment AI Performance Monitoring
requirements.text: Deployed AI systems are monitored to evaluate the continued reliability and safety of the AI system. Performance metrics are tracked against defined thresholds and deviations trigger review and response.
requirements.scope: AI deployers and operators

controls.description: Implement production monitoring for AI system performance, drift, and anomalous outputs
Define and test incident response procedures for AI system performance failures

requirements.title: MANAGE 1.1 — AI Risk Treatment Plans
requirements.text: Responses to identified AI risks are planned. Risk response options include avoidance, mitigation, transfer, and acceptance. Risk treatment plans are documented and actioned.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Produce and implement risk treatment plans for all identified AI risks

requirements.title: MANAGE 1.3 — Responses to AI Incidents
requirements.text: Responses to AI risks and incidents follow documented procedures. Incidents are classified, investigated, and remediated in a timely manner. Lessons learned are captured and feed into risk management improvement.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Maintain an AI incident management process with defined classification, escalation, and response procedures

requirements.title: MANAGE 2.2 — AI System Decommissioning
requirements.text: Mechanisms are in place to deactivate, roll back, or decommission AI systems that no longer meet risk tolerance requirements or have demonstrated harmful impacts. Decommissioning plans are documented.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Define and test AI system shutdown and rollback procedures

requirements.title: MANAGE 3.1 — AI Risk and Benefit Communication
requirements.text: AI risks and benefits are communicated to affected parties including users, affected communities, and regulators. Communication is clear, timely, and appropriate to the audience.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Establish communication plans for AI risk reporting to stakeholders

requirements.title: MANAGE 4.1 — AI Risk Management Improvement
requirements.text: AI risk management processes are continually improved based on monitoring results, incident learnings, and changes in the AI landscape. Improvement actions are documented and tracked.
requirements.scope: All AI developing and deploying organisations

controls.description: Conduct periodic reviews of AI risk management effectiveness and implement improvements
